channel.title: ResumeElite resume blog
channel.description: Practical guides to writing a resume: ATS parsing, summaries that are not filler, action verbs, keywords, resume length and the mistakes that cost interviews.

item.title: How to write a resume with no experience
item.description: You have more material than you think. The problem is usually that it is described too vaguely to count.

item.title: Resume vs CV: what the difference actually is
item.description: Two documents and one naming collision. The naming causes more trouble than the documents do.

item.title: Should you put a photo on your resume?
item.description: It is a regional convention, not a matter of taste -- and getting it wrong reads as not knowing the market.

item.title: How long should a resume be?
item.description: The page count is not the problem. What fills the pages is.

item.title: Resume keywords: how to match a job description properly
item.description: Mirroring the posting's vocabulary is legitimate and effective. Padding a keyword list is neither.

item.title: Resume action verbs that actually change the sentence
item.description: A stronger verb only helps if the rest of the sentence carries a result. Here is the list, and the structure it goes into.

item.title: Professional summary examples that are not filler
item.description: Most summaries are three lines of adjectives that describe nobody. Here is what to write instead.

item.title: How to write a resume in 2026
item.description: The whole process, in order, with the decisions that actually change the outcome and the ones that do not.

item.title: How ATS software actually reads your resume
item.description: Less mysterious and less ruthless than the internet suggests -- but there are specific ways to break it, and they are worth knowing.

item.title: 17 resume mistakes, and the fix for each
item.description: Ordered by damage done, not by how often the internet mentions them.
